newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Zaire's Mobutu in Morocco to meet old ally.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu in Morocco to meet old ally.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, whose country is being shaken by a rebel advance, arrived in Morocco on Monday for a three-day working visit during which he is expected to hold talks with long-time ally King Hassan.
Mobutu, who has been convalescing in France from prostate cancer surgery, was welcomed at Rabat airport by Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and other government officials, eyewitnesses said.
The Zairean president, wearing a blue suit and his trademark leopardskin hat, carried his traditional cane in his hand as he left his white DC-8 jet. He made no statement.
"President Mobutu will spend a three-day working visit in Morocco and confer with his majesty King Hassan on issues of mutual interest," a Moroccan official told Reuters. He did not elaborate.

A Western diplomat said King Hassan was expected to discuss the latest developments in Zaire, including the reported seizure on Monday of the southeastern mining town and lake port of Kalemie, birthplace of rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

Kalemie fell late on Sunday after heavy fighting between government troops and rebels of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), military sources in the region told Reuters earlier.
Moroccan troops in 1977 took part in putting down a secessionist uprising in the southern province of Shaba after Zairean forces failed to make any headway.
The royal armed forces also relieved French and Belgian paratroops giving support to the Zairean authorities in the mining town of Kolwezi the following year.
Since he underwent prostate surgery in Switzerland on August 22, Mobutu has spent most of his time in his palatial French Riviera residence at Roquebrune-Cap Martin.

He returned briefly to Zaire in December and ordered an army reorganisation to launch a counter-offensive against the rebels near the border with Rwanda and Uganda, but flew back to France for further medical checks.
Mobutu is expected to leave Morocco for Kinshasa on Thursday at 7 a.m (0700 GMT), a Moroccan official said.
